messages.subject: correlations?
parts:
Dear list,

I am trying to use lavaan for teaching purpose. Concerning correlations, I know people here have discussed this before, I just want to make sure my understanding is correct:

for correlation between two variables x and y,

1. if I define x as a factor, y as numeric (continuous) in R, depending on the number of the categories of x, lavaan will calculate (point-)biserial/polyserial correlation;

2. if both x and y are defined as factors, lavaan will calculate tetrachoric/phi/polychoric correlation.

Is that right?

Best regards,

ya

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: correlations?
parts:
1. if I define x as a factor, y as numeric (continuous) in R, depending on the number of the categories of x, lavaan will calculate (point-)biserial/polyserial correlation;

2. if both x and y are defined as factors, lavaan will calculate tetrachoric/phi/polychoric correlation.

Is that right?

Assuming by factor you mean c("ordered","factor"), it depends whether your model treats both both x and y as random variables.
  • For exogenous observed variables, lavaan calculates Phi (just a Pearson correlation between dummy codes) or point-*serial (Pearson correlation between dummy codes and other exogenous continuous predictors) from sample statistics and just treats them as fixed (if fixed.x = TRUE), or estimates them (if fixed.x = FALSE).
  • For endogenous variables, lavaan instead estimates *choric or *serial correlations, which make the assumption of a normally distributed latent item response behind each observed ordered factor. 

So if you are literally just running a "model" to estimate a bivariate correlation between 2 variables (with no other modeled effects), then I think you would have to treat them as single-indicators of factors (and therefore endogenous), whose (model-implied) correlation will be estimated.
